result.title: StreamDuo: A Live Commentator and a Research Agent for Unseen Games
result.summary: Streaming video LLMs can now commentate live gameplay, but they are trained and tested on the same games. We study cross-game streaming commentary, in which a model trained on one game commentates games it has never seen, and find that current commentators transfer their timing but not their knowledge of the game world. We propose StreamDuo, which pairs a trainable commentator with a frozen research agent that reads the wiki of the game being played. When the commentator sees something it cannot name, it sends the current frames, and the research agent returns a few wiki entries two seconds later while the stream continues. We train only the commentator, on a single game, in two stages. Information-gain labels teach it to ask only where an answer would help it say what the human caster said, and on-policy self-distillation from a copy of itself that sees the ideal answer teaches it to use noisy answers. Trained on Baldur's Gate 3 and tested on ten unseen games, StreamDuo raises entity recall from 0.082 to 0.116 over Proact-VL trained on the same data, cuts source-game leakage from 9.9% to 1.0%, and achieves the best timing and the highest judged liveliness and overall quality among streaming models.

AI.brief_summary: 研究跨游戏直播解说：模型只在一个游戏上训练，却要解说十个未见过的游戏。提出 StreamDuo，将可训练解说器与一个只读当前游戏 wiki 的冻结研究代理配对，用信息增益标签教它在答案有助于说出人类解说内容时才发起查询，并用在线自蒸馏学会使用带噪声的检索答案。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「何时值得查询外部 wiki」的信息增益门控与对噪声证据的使用训练，可供核查 LVR 中 LOOK 决策、证据获取与视觉证据筛选问题；但任务属直播解说应用，未涉及 latent 推理状态。
